en.title: Fresh snow in Courchevel next week: up to 42 cm on the upper slopes (23–29 November 2026)
en.description: Next week's fresh snow in Courchevel: 12–42 cm on the upper slopes and 4–30 cm at the base (23–29 November 2026), best day, best slopes and how sure the forecast is.
en.lede: Next week's snow numbers for Courchevel: 27 cm at the top, 26 cm at mid-mountain, 17 cm at the base, all as the middle of a range for 23–29 November. The top's range runs from 12 to 42 cm, which says as much as the middle value does.

p: This week is the heavy one: 85 cm at the top between 17 and 20 November (range 63–106 cm), 5 cm at the base. Next week's snow falls onto that, which matters more than the size of the second round.

sections.h: What falls where on the Courchevel slopes
p: Read from the top down: 27 cm near 2500 m, 26 cm near 2000 m, 17 cm near 1300 m. The low-to-high spread is 12–42 cm at the top and 4–30 cm at the base.
Day by day, the upper mountain picks up most of it on Wednesday 25 (8 cm, up to 8), Thursday 26 (8 cm, up to 12) and Sunday 29 (6 cm, up to 10). Outside those days expect little more than flurries.

sections.h: Where the good snow will be
p: If you can pick one day, take the one that follows Wednesday 25 November, when 8 cm (up to 8 cm) has landed on the upper mountain.

The snow lies best on Saulire and the high bowls above Courchevel 1850. For the softest turns, look to the north-facing Courchevel side and the tree-lined runs above Le Praz for flat light. Lower down, Le Praz and La Tania at the bottom of the forest runs will be the first to suffer if the air turns mild.
At the base the total drops to 17 cm, roughly half of the top. Expect heavier, wetter snow on the lower runs and a snow line that wanders around village level on the mildest day.
Courchevel's grooming is famous, which means fresh snow is pisted fast: early lifts matter.
The range is wide: 12 cm in the low case, 42 cm in the high one. That is normal a week ahead. The timing is more reliable than the total.
A forecast seven to thirteen days out is a trend, not a ticket.
Same week, same measure (top of each resort): Méribel (5 km away) 28 cm; La Plagne (13 km away) 28 cm; Val Thorens (14 km away) 30 cm. Courchevel itself: 27 cm.
Nothing to separate them on snow alone; the choice comes down to the terrain you want.

advice: Off the groomed runs, new snow means new avalanche risk: the French avalanche bulletin (BERA) for the massif is the reference.
Opening dates are the resort's call; our numbers only say how much snow is coming.
Plan around the top's 27 cm, and keep the high case of 42 cm as a bonus.
